statement: The province should introduce a wealth tax on the largest personal fortunes.

passages.title: Hansard — Feb 18 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 118
passages.quote: I’d be very surprised if MLAs from rural communities wouldn’t join me in supporting the need for tax fairness. That’s why we proposed a wealth tax package to the government — one that would address both inequality and the deficit, one that the government refused to engage with, refused to even look at. Yet we have a $13 billion deficit coming up, and we’re not prepared to look at the tax policy side of the equation. That is just irresponsible.

passages.title: Hansard — May 25 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 183
passages.quote: I’ll just share that I also worry about the impacts of fast fashion and am a big believer in pre-loved clothing and shoes, and so on. It remains true that those are also PST-exempt. I think the member mentioned that they were talking to someone who I believe has a textile factory, if I understood correctly, and was worried that the PST changes might deter that person from upgrading their machinery, I’m assuming. We do have a manufacturing tax credit that is introduced in Budget 2026, of 15 percent.

passages.title: BC Hansard 2026-05-28 pm, Issue 188 (Komoks Treaty Act third reading, Conservative speeches)
passages.quote: Well, that’s on $20 billion of personal income tax that they decided that they needed to change the tax rate on, to go up for everybody on their first $51,000 of income. They’re not content with that. This Premier decided to freeze the income tax brackets as well for three years, so they can collect more tax off of every single British Columbian for the next three years as people get more income. If they have wage settlements or wage growth, they have frozen the basic personal tax exemption for the next three years.

passages.title: BC Hansard 2026-05-28 pm, Issue 188 (Komoks Treaty Act third reading, Conservative speeches)
passages.quote: They did freeze basic personal exemptions for three years. They have frozen the tax brackets for three years. They did raise the personal income tax on the lowest first $51,000, $50,000 plus of earnings from 5.06 percent to 5.6 percent. I would love for the Premier to show me where any of that is not factually accurate.

passages.title: Hansard — Feb 18 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 118
passages.quote: Why are we afraid to look at everybody paying their fair share? We would argue, though, that tax reform needs to go further than income. It needs to include wealth, because it’s not the doctors, the engineers and the developers earning $200,000 a year, the lawyers, that are driving this inequality. It’s those who are building huge stores of wealth, who are refusing to invest in improving our productivity, those who are crowding out small businesses.
